target: fatal accidents involving Boeing commercial jets

evidence.observation: Fatal Western-built jet hull losses include Ethiopian 737-800, Air India Express 737-800, Airblue A321, AeroUnion A300, Aires 737-700, Afriqiyah A330, UPS 747-400 and Henan EMB-190. The Boeing target members are Ethiopian, Air India Express, Aires and UPS.

evidence.scope: worldwide commercial jet fleet under documented Boeing definitions
evidence.observation: The 2010 annual table independently reconciles the commercial-jet events and explicitly preserves external fatalities. Its annual total is 555 onboard fatalities and one external fatality; no additional Boeing target event is introduced by the external-fatality check.
evidence.use: independent annual reconciliation and external-fatality control

evidence.publisher: Lebanese Directorate General of Civil Aviation
evidence.observation: Competent authority investigation of Ethiopian flight ET409, Boeing 737-800 ET-ANB, fatal accident after departure from Beirut.

evidence.publisher: Directorate General of Civil Aviation, India
evidence.source_title: Air India Express IX812 accident investigation
evidence.observation: Air India Express flight 812, Boeing 737-800 VT-AXV, overran the runway at Mangalore; 158 fatalities. NTSB accredited-representative record identifies DGCA India as the investigating authority.
Competent authority report identifies scheduled commercial Boeing 737-700 HK-4682 accident at San Andres.

evidence.publisher: General Civil Aviation Authority, United Arab Emirates
evidence.observation: Competent authority investigated UPS flight 6, Boeing 747-44AF N571UP; both pilots died after an in-flight cargo fire and loss of control.

completeness_assessment.reason: The fatal Western-built jet universe is explicitly enumerated, all Boeing target memberships are mapped, each Boeing candidate has competent-authority evidence, Boeing independently reconciles the annual commercial-jet table including external fatalities, and no unresolved target-taxonomy boundary affects a Boeing 2010 case.
